The high-window relation criterion is deliberately stated with a residue-fibre

actual kernel of the multiplication presentation, proves it finite, and identifies
its spanning condition with fibrewise injectivity of the injectivized map.

Flatness of the target cokernel implies that condition.  Conversely, the landed
flattening criterion shows that the condition implies target-cokernel flatness.
Consequently, merely choosing the actual kernel does not evade the nonreduced-base

No fibrewise image-persistence statement is used as a substitute for this law.
-/

section KernelSpan

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
  [Module R M] [Module R N]

/-- Kernel spanning after base change is equivalent to injectivity after first
dividing the source by the global kernel.  This is pure linear algebra and holds
for an arbitrary coefficient module `A`.

The forward direction lifts through the right-exact base change of the quotient
map.  The reverse direction observes that an element in the fibre kernel has zero
image in the fibre of the injectivization, hence already lies in the fibre image
of the global kernel. -/
theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor A) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker f).subtype.rTensor A) ↔
      Function.Injective
        (((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A) := by
  let L := LinearMap.ker f
  have hcomp : f.rTensor A =
      (L.liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A ∘ₗ L.mkQ.rTensor A := by
    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
  have hexact : Function.Exact (L.subtype.rTensor A) (L.mkQ.rTensor A) :=
    rTensor_exact A (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ L) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L)
  constructor
  · intro hspan
    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
    intro w hw
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.rTensor_surjective A
      (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
    have hfx : f.rTensor A x = 0 := by
      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
      exact hw
    have hx := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker] at hx
    exact hx
  · intro hinj x hx
    have hzero : L.mkQ.rTensor A x = 0 := by
      apply hinj
      rw [map_zero]
      have hfx := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx
      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply] at hfx
      exact hfx
    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    exact hzero

-- Elaborating the quotient injectivization through tensor purity exceeds the default budget.
/-- Flatness of the target cokernel forces the fibre kernel to be generated by
the base-changed global kernel.  Indeed, the injectivization
`M ⧸ ker δ → N` has cokernel `N ⧸ range δ`; flatness of that cokernel makes the
injectivization universally injective. -/
theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_of_flat_range_quotient
    (δ : M →ₗ[R] N)
    [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    LinearMap.ker (δ.rTensor A) ≤
      LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.rTensor A) := by
  apply (ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective δ A).mpr
  set fbar := (LinearMap.ker δ).liftQ δ le_rfl with hfbar
  have hfbar_inj : Function.Injective fbar := by
    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, hfbar]
    exact Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot' _ δ rfl
  have hexact : Function.Exact fbar (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ := by
    rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.ker_mkQ, hfbar, Submodule.range_liftQ]
  have hleft : Function.Injective (fbar.lTensor A) :=
    LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
      (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
      fbar hfbar_inj hexact A
  exact (LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj (M := A) (f := fbar)).mp hleft

end KernelSpan

    16	The recursive high-window relation at a successor is generated by multiplying the
    17	preceding relation by the finite multiplier window.  This file records the chart

    76	private theorem span_range_comp_surjective
    77	    {R B M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    78	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    79	    (f : M →ₗ[R] B) (e : N →ₗ[R] M) (he : Function.Surjective e) :
    80	    Ideal.span (Set.range (f.comp e)) = Ideal.span (Set.range f) := by
    81	  apply le_antisymm
    82	  · refine Ideal.span_le.mpr ?_
    83	    rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
    84	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨e x, rfl⟩
    85	  · refine Ideal.span_le.mpr ?_
    86	    rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
    87	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := he x
    88	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨y, rfl⟩

    94	    Ideal.span (Set.range (f.comp (Submodule.map e N).subtype)) =
    95	      Ideal.span (Set.range ((f.comp e).comp N.subtype)) := by
    96	  let em := e.submoduleMap N

    98	    Ideal.span (Set.range (f.comp (Submodule.map e N).subtype)) =
    99	        Ideal.span (Set.range ((f.comp (Submodule.map e N).subtype).comp em)) := by
   100	      symm
   101	      exact span_range_comp_surjective
   102	        (f := f.comp (Submodule.map e N).subtype) (e := em)
   103	          (LinearMap.submoduleMap_surjective e N)
   104	    _ = Ideal.span (Set.range ((f.comp e).comp N.subtype)) := by
   105	      have hmaps :

   107	            (f.comp e).comp N.subtype := by

   109	        intro x

     9	/-!
    10	# DD-4 redesign: the valid flat-range fibre bridge
    11	
    12	Let `P ≤ M` be an `R`-linear range and let `L ≤ P`.  There is a canonical exact
    13	sequence `0 → map (L.mkQ) P → M/L → M/P → 0`.
    14	
    15	If `M/P` is `R`-flat, the first map stays injective after tensoring with every
    16	`R`-module.  Consequently, if the image `map (L.mkQ) P` dies in a residue-field
    17	fibre of `M/L`, its own tensor fibre is zero.  The containment `L ≤ P` is essential:
    18	`e ∈ P` alone does not imply `(e) ⊆ P` for an `R`-linear submodule.  For example,
    19	with `R = k`, `M = k[t]`, `P = k · t`, and `e = t`, one has `e ∈ P` but `t² ∉ P`.
    20	No ideal-flatness claim is made here.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    25	
    26	universe uR uM u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    29	open scoped TensorProduct
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	namespace FlatRangeBridge
    34	
    35	variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
    36	variable {M : Type uM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    37	
    38	/-- The image of `P` in the quotient by `L`. -/
    39	noncomputable def imageInQuotient (L P : Submodule R M) : Submodule R (M ⧸ L) :=
    40	  Submodule.map L.mkQ P
    41	
    42	/-- Image of a range in a quotient, written as the range of the composite quotient map. -/
    43	lemma imageInQuotient_range (L : Submodule R M) {U : Type*}
    44	    [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U] (f : U →ₗ[R] M) :
    45	    imageInQuotient L (LinearMap.range f) = LinearMap.range (L.mkQ.comp f) := by
    46	  rw [imageInQuotient, ← LinearMap.range_comp]
    47	
    48	/-- The quotient map induced by `L ≤ P`. -/
    49	noncomputable def quotientMapOfLE {L P : Submodule R M} (hLP : L ≤ P) :
    50	    (M ⧸ L) →ₗ[R] (M ⧸ P) :=
    51	  L.liftQ P.mkQ fun x hx => by
    52	    rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
    53	    exact hLP hx
    54	
    55	@[simp]
    56	lemma quotientMapOfLE_mk {L P : Submodule R M} (hLP : L ≤ P) (x : M) :
    57	    quotientMapOfLE hLP (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk x := by
    58	  rw [quotientMapOfLE, Submodule.liftQ_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply]
    59	
    60	lemma quotientMapOfLE_surjective {L P : Submodule R M} (hLP : L ≤ P) :
    61	    Function.Surjective (quotientMapOfLE hLP) := by
    62	  intro y
    63	  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective P y
    64	  exact ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk x, quotientMapOfLE_mk hLP x⟩
    65	
    66	lemma ker_quotientMapOfLE {L P : Submodule R M} (hLP : L ≤ P) :
    67	    LinearMap.ker (quotientMapOfLE hLP) = imageInQuotient L P := by
    68	  ext y
    69	  induction y using Submodule.Quotient.induction_on with
    70	  | _ x =>
    71	    rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, quotientMapOfLE_mk, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
    72	    constructor
    73	    · intro hx
    74	      exact ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    75	    · rintro ⟨z, hz, hzx⟩
    76	      have hzx' : x - z ∈ L := by
    77	        exact (Submodule.Quotient.eq _).mp hzx.symm
    78	      simpa only [sub_add_cancel] using P.add_mem (hLP hzx') hz
    79	
    80	lemma exact_imageInQuotient_subtype_quotientMapOfLE {L P : Submodule R M}
    81	    (hLP : L ≤ P) :
    82	    Function.Exact (imageInQuotient L P).subtype (quotientMapOfLE hLP) := by
    83	  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.range_subtype, ker_quotientMapOfLE hLP]
    84	
    85	/-- Flatness of `M/P` makes the inclusion of the image in `M/L` universally injective. -/
    86	lemma imageInQuotient_lTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient
    87	    {L P : Submodule R M} (hLP : L ≤ P) [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ P)]
    88	    (A : Type*) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    89	    Function.Injective ((imageInQuotient L P).subtype.lTensor A) := by
    90	  exact LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
    91	    (quotientMapOfLE hLP) (quotientMapOfLE_surjective hLP)
    92	    (imageInQuotient L P).subtype (Submodule.injective_subtype _)
    93	    (exact_imageInQuotient_subtype_quotientMapOfLE hLP) A
    94	
    95	/-- If the image dies in an arbitrary fibre, its tensor fibre is subsingleton. -/
    96	lemma subsingleton_imageInQuotient_tensor_of_flat_quotient
    97	    {L P : Submodule R M} (hLP : L ≤ P) [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ P)]
    98	    (A : Type*) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A]
    99	    (hzero : ∀ n : imageInQuotient L P, ∀ a : A,
   100	      ((n : M ⧸ L) ⊗ₜ[R] a) = 0) :

     8	/-!

    10	
    11	The chart reading map is only `R`-linear.  Its `R`-linear range is therefore not the ideal
    12	generated by its readings in the chart ring `B = Γ(V)`.  This file records the actual
    13	`B`-ideal and the scalar-extension maps that present its underlying `B`-modules:
    14	
    15	* `chartReadIdeal K b = Ideal.span (range (chartReadMap K b))`;
    16	* `chartReadIdealMap K b : B ⊗[R] K →ₗ[B] B`, whose range is `chartReadIdeal K b`;
    17	* `chartIdealColengthModule K b s`, the image of `chartReadIdeal K b` in
    18	  `B ⧸ Ideal.span {read s}`;
    19	* `chartIdealColengthMap K b s`, whose range is that image.
    20	
    21	The last module agrees with the previously landed `chartColengthModule`.  No flatness or
    22	fibre-injectivity statement is made here: those properties for the `R`-linear range do not
    23	automatically pass to this `B`-ideal.

    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

    29	universe uR uB uM uN u

    34	namespace LinearMap
    35	
    36	/-- The range of scalar extension is the span, over the new scalar ring, of the original
    37	range.  In particular, this is the precise map presenting the ideal generated by an
    38	`R`-linear family of elements of an `R`-algebra. -/
    39	theorem range_liftBaseChange_eq_span
    40	    {R : Type uR} {B : Type uB} {M : Type uM} {N : Type uN}
    41	    [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    42	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    43	    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower R B N]
    44	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    45	    LinearMap.range (LinearMap.liftBaseChange B f) =
    46	      Submodule.span B (Set.range f) := by
    47	  apply le_antisymm
    48	  · rintro y ⟨x, rfl⟩
    49	    induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    50	    | zero => exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    51	    | add x y hx hy =>
    52	        simpa only [map_add] using Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy
    53	    | tmul b m =>
    54	        rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul]
    55	        exact Submodule.smul_mem _ b (Submodule.subset_span ⟨m, rfl⟩)
    56	  · rw [Submodule.span_le]
    57	    rintro _ ⟨m, rfl⟩
    58	    exact ⟨(1 : B) ⊗ₜ[R] m, by
    59	      rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]⟩

    73	/-- The genuine chart-ring ideal generated by the readings of `K`.  This is generally larger
    74	than the `R`-linear range of `chartReadMap K b`. -/
    75	noncomputable def chartReadIdeal
    76	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool) :
    77	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) :=
    78	  Ideal.span (Set.range (chartReadMap K b))
    79	
    80	/-- The minimal scalar-extension map presenting the ideal generated by the chart readings:
    81	`c ⊗ ψ ↦ c · read(ψ)`. -/
    82	noncomputable def chartReadIdealMap
    83	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool) :
    84	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⊗[R] ↥K →ₗ[Γ(relCurve C R,
    85	      relPinnedChart C R π b)] Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) :=
    86	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) (chartReadMap K b)

    89	/-- The range of `chartReadIdealMap` is exactly the genuine chart-reading ideal. -/
    90	theorem range_chartReadIdealMap
    91	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool) :

    95	      (R := R) (B := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    96	      (M := ↥K) (N := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    97	      (chartReadMap K b))

    99	/-- The image of the genuine chart-reading ideal in the colength ring
   100	`B ⧸ Ideal.span {read s}`.  Equivalently, this is `(chartReadIdeal K b + (read s)) / (read s)`,
   101	viewed as a `B`-submodule of the quotient. -/
   102	noncomputable def chartIdealColengthModule
   103	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   104	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   105	    Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   106	      (Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
   107	        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s}) :=
   108	  Submodule.map
   109	    (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   110	      (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap
   111	    (chartReadIdeal K b)
   112	
   113	/-- The ideal-theoretic colength module is exactly the previously defined `B`-span of the
   114	classes of the chart readings. -/
   115	theorem chartIdealColengthModule_eq_chartColengthModule
   116	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   117	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   118	    chartIdealColengthModule K b s = chartColengthModule K b s := by
   119	  rw [chartIdealColengthModule, chartReadIdeal, Submodule.map_span, chartColengthModule]
   120	  congr 1
   121	  ext x
   122	  constructor
   123	  · rintro ⟨_, ⟨m, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   124	    exact ⟨m, rfl⟩
   125	  · rintro ⟨m, rfl⟩
   126	    exact ⟨chartReadMap K b m, ⟨m, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   127	
   128	/-- The scalar-extension presentation of the chart-reading ideal after quotienting by the
   129	chosen section. -/
   130	noncomputable def chartIdealColengthMap
   131	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   132	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   133	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⊗[R] ↥K →ₗ[Γ(relCurve C R,

   135	      (Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
   136	        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s}) :=
   137	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   138	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap.comp
   139	      (chartReadMap K b))

   141	set_option maxHeartbeats 2400000 in
   142	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   143	/-- The range of the quotient scalar-extension map is the ideal-theoretic colength module. -/
   144	theorem range_chartIdealColengthMap
   145	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   146	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   147	    LinearMap.range (chartIdealColengthMap K b s) = chartIdealColengthModule K b s := by
   148	  rw [chartIdealColengthModule_eq_chartColengthModule]
   149	  simpa only [chartIdealColengthMap, chartColengthModule] using

   151	      (R := R) (B := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
   152	      (M := ↥K)
   153	      (N := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
   154	        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})
   155	      ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R
   156	        (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap.comp
   157	          (chartReadMap K b)))

    10	/-!
    11	# DD-4 redesign: purity of the genuine chart ideal
    12	
    13	The reading map has an `R`-linear range, while the divisor is cut out by the
    14	`B`-ideal generated by that range.  This file records the elementary purity
    15	bridge for the latter.  Flatness of `B / J` over `R` makes the inclusion
    16	`J ↪ B` universally injective; in particular, after tensoring with a residue
    17	field, a principal subideal of `J` can be compared inside the ambient fibre.
    18	
    19	No geometric generation statement is asserted here.  Callers still have to
    20	provide the appropriate fibrewise (usually single-point) generation input.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open scoped TensorProduct
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	namespace IdealPurity
    32	
    33	variable {R B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    34	
    35	/-! ## The ideal as the kernel of its quotient -/
    36	
    37	@[simp]
    38	theorem restrictScalars_ker_quotient
    39	    (J : Ideal B) :
    40	    LinearMap.ker (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap = J.restrictScalars R := by
    41	  ext x
    42	  simp [Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem]
    43	
    44	/-! ## Universal injectivity of a flat ideal inclusion -/
    45	
    46	/-- If `B / J` is `R`-flat, the inclusion of the genuine ideal `J` into `B`
    47	remains injective after tensoring with any `R`-module. -/
    48	theorem subtype_lTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient
    49	    (J : Ideal B) [Module.Flat R (B ⧸ J)]
    50	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    51	    Function.Injective ((J.restrictScalars R).subtype.lTensor A) := by
    52	  apply LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
    53	    (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).toLinearMap
    54	    Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective
    55	    (J.restrictScalars R).subtype
    56	    (Submodule.injective_subtype _)
    57	  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, restrictScalars_ker_quotient]
    58	  exact (Submodule.range_subtype _).symm
    59	
    60	/-- The same purity statement in the right-tensor orientation. -/
    61	theorem subtype_rTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient
    62	    (J : Ideal B) [Module.Flat R (B ⧸ J)]
    63	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    64	    Function.Injective ((J.restrictScalars R).subtype.rTensor A) := by
    65	  exact ((J.restrictScalars R).subtype.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj A).mp
    66	    (subtype_lTensor_injective_of_flat_quotient (R := R) (B := B) J A)
    67	
    68	end IdealPurity
    69	
    70	end AlgebraicGeometry

    44	/-- **`baseChange ⟹ rTensor` injectivity transfer**: the left base change `A ⊗ g` and the
    45	right tensor `g ⊗ A` are conjugate by `TensorProduct.comm` (an `R`-linear equivalence), so
    46	injectivity of the former transfers to the latter.  Used to move a residue-fibre
    47	injectivity computed on the natural `κ(p)`-space `κ(p) ⊗ M` onto the `.rTensor κ(p)` shape
    48	the carve framework consumes. -/
    49	theorem rTensor_injective_of_baseChange_injective
    50	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    51	    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    52	    (g : M →ₗ[R] N) (h : Function.Injective (LinearMap.baseChange A g)) :
    53	    Function.Injective (g.rTensor A) := by
    54	  have key : ∀ z : M ⊗[R] A, (TensorProduct.comm R N A) (g.rTensor A z)
    55	      = (LinearMap.baseChange A g) ((TensorProduct.comm R M A) z) := by
    56	    intro z
    57	    induction z with
    58	    | zero => simp
    59	    | tmul m a =>
    60	        simp [LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, TensorProduct.comm_tmul, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul]
    61	    | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
    62	  intro x y hxy
    63	  have hbc : (LinearMap.baseChange A g) ((TensorProduct.comm R M A) x)
    64	      = (LinearMap.baseChange A g) ((TensorProduct.comm R M A) y) := by
    65	    rw [← key, ← key, hxy]
    66	  exact (TensorProduct.comm R M A).injective (h hbc)
    67	
    68	/-- **The range-inclusion residue fibre stays injective**: from injectivity of the left
    69	base change `A ⊗ f`, the residue fibre `(range f).subtype ⊗ A` is injective.  Factor
    70	`f = (range f).subtype ∘ f.rangeRestrict` with `f.rangeRestrict` surjective, tensor by `A`,
    71	and cancel the surjective factor. -/
    72	theorem range_subtype_rTensor_injective_of_baseChange_injective
    73	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    74	    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    75	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (h : Function.Injective (LinearMap.baseChange A f)) :

    79	  have hcomp_eq : (LinearMap.range f).subtype ∘ₗ f.rangeRestrict = f :=

    95	    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) :

   102	    | tmul a m =>
   103	        rw [Submodule.mem_comap, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul]
   104	        exact Submodule.tmul_mem_baseChange_of_mem a (LinearMap.mem_range_self φ m)
   105	    | add x y hx hy =>
   106	        rw [Submodule.mem_comap, map_add]
   107	        exact Submodule.add_mem _ (Submodule.mem_comap.1 hx) (Submodule.mem_comap.1 hy)
   108	  · rw [Submodule.baseChange_eq_span, Submodule.span_le]
   109	    rintro _ ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
   110	    obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := hy
   111	    exact ⟨(1 : A) ⊗ₜ[R] m, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, TensorProduct.mk_apply]⟩

## Why I Stopped

The remaining statement is not merely technical. For every residue field and every high-window multiplication map, one must prove

```text
ker(multiplication) = range(Koszul boundary).
```

Only `range ⊆ ker` and multiplication surjectivity are currently proved. The missing reverse inclusion is precisely a relative Gotzmann/first-syzygy theorem, equivalently the unproved finrank lower bound at [DivSchemeHighWindowKoszul.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowKoszul.lean:296).

Choosing the actual global kernel does not bypass this: [DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:254) proves that its fibre-base-change law is equivalent to the desired quotient flatness, so that argument would be circular.

The old Jacobian flattening theorem changes the base to locally closed rank strata and its Quot endpoint is still sorry-backed. The redesign theorem proves flatness only for the `RZ`-linear reading range, not the larger chart ideal. Neither is a drop-in completion.

Therefore representability is not yet fully formalized. The next substantive task is proving that relative first-syzygy rank estimate, or deliberately porting the full flattening-stratification route.
